name: Linen (flax, Linum usitatissimum), plain-woven
aliases: muslin (in the design's looser sense of a fine plain weave)
summary: Cloth woven from the long bast fibres of the flax plant: strong, slubbed, matt with a quiet lustre. In the Reserve it is the natural, unbleached linen stretched on boards in the fumed-oak frames of the sliding picture screens; in the Salon's bay 4 it is the blind in the lantern that softens the daylight.

whyAnAccent.text: The material-language board groups the cloths with the timber: 'D · The oak, and what it carries: timber, leather, silk, felt'. Each cloth is declared an accent of the oak family (D-014); the Architect may overturn this reading.
whyAnAccent.source: MuseeVision/Journal/Decisions.md, D-014 (Matter: every substance carries its family; an accent names its core family); plan/canvas/MaterialsOther.dc.html, section 'D · The oak, and what it carries'

formation.how: Flax stems are retted (bacteria decompose the pectin that binds the fibre bundles), scutched to break away the woody core, and heckled with combs to separate the long line fibres from the short tow; the line is spun and woven. Its yarn carries slubs, small soft irregular lumps along its length; the cloth is strong and absorbent, dries fast and wrinkles easily.

slubs.text: Small, soft, irregular lumps occur randomly along the yarn's length.

strength.text: Up to three times stronger than cotton; poor elasticity, so it wrinkles.

processing.text: Retting (bacteria decompose the pectin), scutching, heckling.

clothModelLinenPlain.note: Fitted to measured BRDFs of a plain-weave linen (Table II, row a): twisted threads in both directions; linen gives a smooth reflection and mostly isotropic volume scattering. A carries that sample's dye.

optics.blindTransmittance: The bay-4 blind is a diffusing transmitter: daylight from Giverny's sky passes through one layer. Its transmittance is unverified (the first build used 0.40 as a hand value).

physical.note: Fibre facts are under formation; fibre density and moisture regain are unverified.

absorptionByOctave.source: Table 'Sound Absorption Coefficients', http://usenclosure.com/Diffraction%20Graphs/Sound%20Absorption%20Coefficients.pdf (the same table the white group cites for plaster; it names no primary source)
absorptionByOctave.conditions: row 'Light Velour, 10 oz/sq yd, hung straight, in contact with wall': the nearest tabulated case for a thin cloth laid flat on a hard backing

acoustic.note: For the screens' linen on boards; the lantern blind is overhead behind glass and is not an acoustic surface of the room.

screens.text: Each screen: a panel 5.0 m long, 0.10 m thick and 3.33 m tall, a fumed-oak frame round two fields of natural linen stretched on boards.

sensitivity.text: High light sensitivity (ISO Blue Wool 1-3) covers most plant extracts and hence most historic bright dyes, insect dyes, most early synthetic colours, and textiles; UV causes yellowing, chalking and weakening, and prolonged exposure weakens and fragments most wool, cotton, silk and paper.
sensitivity.source: Michalski, S. (2018) Agent of deterioration: light, ultraviolet and infrared. Canadian Conservation Institute, 2018-05-17, https://www.canada.ca/en/conservation-institute/services/agents-deterioration/light.html

uvLimit.note: traditional museum limit; about 10 uW/lm gives high-sensitivity materials extra protection

conservation.note: Unbleached linen is undyed; its risk is weakening and yellowing, not fading.

physicalMaterial.note: Not walked on. No friction is sourced.

uses.where: the Reserve: both faces of the 36 sliding picture screens
uses.note: works hang 2 cm off the linen on bronze rods from a bronze rail

uses.where: the Salon, bay 4: the blind in the lantern ('a curtained room')
uses.note: the board heads it 'muslin' and describes 'a linen blind in the lantern'; this record reads it as a fine plain-weave linen

notMatter: A canvas's linen (face, tacking edges, back) is Art's support, not this record's.
photograph: Unbleached linen: a grey-beige to oatmeal ground with darker slubs and thicker threads scattered through it.
Stretched on boards: flat, tight, with the weave visible at arm's length and a fine grid of light and shade at grazing light.
In the lantern: a glowing, shadowless panel with the weave faintly visible against the sky.

evidence.shows: A slubbed plain weave at 0.3 m: relief and slubs such as a linen shows; grey, so no colour evidence.
